Each Artemis launch costs about 4 to 5 billion dollars, funded primarily by the United States through NASA with support from international partners like the European Space Agency. 
It is less than half a percent of federal spending, aimed at building long term lunar infrastructure and advanced technology.

The Starship descends back to Earth and lands vertically on its pad, completing one of the most complex maneuvers in modern engineering. Bringing a 120 ton vehicle back from space and landing it precisely is one of the key breakthroughs making fully reusable spaceflight possible.SpaceEve6K views · 5h ago0:45What once sounded impossible is becoming reality. Companies like SpaceX are developing systems to catch returning rocket boosters midair, reducing wear and enabling rapid reuse. If perfected, this could redefine how rockets are recovered and launched again.SpaceEve50.4K views · 8h ago0:21A major milestone for student engineering. Built by SC Rocketry, the Stewart engine has successfully completed another double firing inside a skeletal test stand, producing up to 40 kN of thrust. It still holds the record as the most powerful liquid rocket engine ever built and tested by a university team, showing how advanced student rocketry has become.SpaceEve11.4K views · 10h ago0:20Before docking with the International Space Station, the Space Shuttle performed a 360-degree backflip maneuver. This allowed astronauts on the ISS to photograph all 24,000 heat shield tiles, ensuring there was no damage before reentry. A critical safety check after lessons learned from past missions.SpaceEve4.1K views · 13h ago0:24Training for the next step beyond Artemis II. Christina Koch is preparing for future missions like Artemis IV, where astronauts will return to the lunar surface and begin building a long-term presence. Every step now is preparation for living and working on the Moon.SpaceEve24.5K views · 1d ago0:53After traveling beyond the Moon and back, the Artemis II capsule is finally opened in the ocean. Rescue teams move in as the crew prepares to step out after one of the most historic journeys in decades. This is where the mission truly ends and Earth welcomes them back.SpaceEve49.3K views · 1d ago0:17Captured in real time, this footage shows the extreme conditions of Artemis II reentry, with plasma forming as the capsule interacts with Earth’s atmosphere. Filmed by SEN, this perspective reveals details of heat, speed, and atmospheric physics rarely seen this clearly from orbit.SpaceEve232.4K views · 1d ago0:15A haunting final transmission. The Venera program captured this image from the surface of Venus moments before extreme heat and pressure destroyed the spacecraft. With temperatures above 460°C, nothing survives here for long.SpaceEve36.9K views · 3d ago0:37A journey into the unknown. The Huygens probe captured this footage as it descended through the thick atmosphere of Titan, Saturn’s largest moon.
